subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for the active memory plugin, or keep file scanning and watching owned by each backend/plugin?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent public SDK shape and the local-file exposure boundary need maintainer product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
options.body: Design a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit file-scope consent, event semantics, cleanup ownership, and compatibility tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep scanning plugin-owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may use current list/read helpers but must own their own watchers, indexing, deletion, and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Fold into a broader backend contract
options.body: Defer this request until maintainers decide the larger memory backend contract for ingestion, search, read, writeback, and status ownership.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
recommendation.body: Design a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit file-scope consent, event semantics, cleanup ownership, and compatibility tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across memory SDK, memory host helpers, and memory-core scanner/watcher ownership.
